question: Can `hermit run` around a Nix derivation's builder make a non-reproducible build byte-identical; what is the minimum hermit flag-set that does it on this host; does it work on real nixpkgs packages; and how does a nixpkgs consumer opt in only the packages that need it?

hermit_findings_for_product.summary: detcore answers getuid/geteuid/getgid/getegid with a constant 0 in both namespace modes, but the process cannot back it. GNU tar then attempts ownership restoration and fails: EPERM under --no-namespace (no user namespace at all), EINVAL under --tmp=/tmp (user namespace maps exactly one uid).
hermit_findings_for_product.measured_impact: 4/4 tarball-sourced nixpkgs packages (hello, which, bc, figlet) fail in unpackPhase under the wrap
suggested_fixes: map a wider uid range in the user namespace
virtualize chown/fchown to no-op-success when the guest believes it is root
do not virtualize uid to 0 when sharing the host filesystem

hermit_findings_for_product.summary: Two measured hangs in guest pipe wakeup, each with ZERO accumulated CPU. (1) cmake configure blocks in epoll_wait(epfd=3, maxevents=1024, timeout=-1) on pipes to a compiler-probe child that has exited; /proc/<pid>/wchan = do_epoll_wait. (2) figlet's stdenv fixupPhase: the guest builder bash blocks in read(fd 0, buf, 1) on pipe:[329546543] (also held on saved fd 63) with NO children alive; wchan = anon_pipe_read, TIME 00:00:00 after 29 minutes.
hermit_findings_for_product.reproducer: harness/cmake-hang-repro.sh (3-line CMakeLists.txt): native rc=0 wall=1s; hermit rc=124 wall=90s with no output
hermit_findings_for_product.measured_impact: Hang 1 puts every cmake-based nixpkgs package out of reach, including lensfun -- the one real on-machine-nondeterministic package found. Hang 2 blocks stdenv fixupPhase, which nearly every package runs. Together they are why N=0.
hermit_findings_for_product.suggested_fix: audit detcore's pipe readiness/EOF delivery for both epoll registration and blocking read when the writer exits
hermit_findings_for_product.claim_strength: The two hangs are measured from /proc on live processes. A SHARED root cause is a HYPOTHESIS, not established: one waits in epoll_wait and the other in a blocking read, and a bash `while read` holding the pipe on a saved fd has its own idioms. Defensible statement: hermit does not deliver pipe readiness/EOF to a guest reader after the writer exits, observed through two different waiting primitives.

hermit_findings_for_product.summary: the default logical clock advances with PMU-read RCB counts; on a host where PMU validation fails the guest-visible clock jitters at nanosecond resolution and breaks output reproducibility for any build that reads a high-resolution clock
hermit_findings_for_product.suggested_fix: fall back to check-in-counted logical time automatically when PMU validation fails, instead of logging an error and continuing with an unreliable counter

hermit_findings_for_product.summary: ~8.4x on a trivial exec, but >200x on real configure phases; this is the actual gate on whole-package determinization, not the nix integration

with --no-rcb-time the logical clock advances a fixed increment per scheduler check-in, so a build whose syscall path varies by one check-in lands one quantum apart. Measured quantum here: 250 ms. Not fixed by --strict, --sequentialize-threads, --target-timeslice, or --max-timeslice disabled.
hermit_findings_for_product.measured_impact: a build baking NANOSECONDS can still differ (nondet-demo-fast: 2 distinct/20); a build baking WHOLE SECONDS cannot (nondet-seconds: 1 distinct/20)
hermit_findings_for_product.suggested_fix: make the guest-visible clock a function of committed deterministic events only, not of the raw check-in count
